files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.Choreography.IChoreographyContext
files.Summary: Per-invocation context handed to a to publish forward or compensation events while preserving correlation identifiers across the chain.

files.Summary: Marker interface identifying a class as a participant in an event-driven choreography saga (the "Event Saga" flavor: no central orchestrator; services react to integration events and publish further events).

files.Summary: Handler contract for choreography saga participants. A class can implement several times, once per event type it reacts to.

files.Summary: Marker interface for any persisted saga instance, regardless of flavor.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.Common.SagaStatus
files.Summary: Defines the possible states of a saga during its lifecycle. Shared by both (orchestration) and (choreography) flavors.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.Common.SagaStep
files.Summary: Represents a single step within an orchestration saga, including its execution state and metadata. Steps are owned by an and executed in declared order; compensation runs in reverse order.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.Common.SagaStepStatus
files.Summary: Defines the possible states of an orchestration saga step during its lifecycle. Used exclusively by ; choreography sagas have no concept of named "steps".

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.ProcessManagers.IProcessManager<TState>

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.ProcessManagers.IProcessManager
files.Summary: Represents a DDD-style orchestration saga ("Process Manager" in Vaughn Vernon's terminology) — a stateful coordinator that groups operations across multiple aggregates within a bounded context, drives them through explicit steps, and performs compensation on failure.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.ProcessManagers.IProcessManagerOrchestrator

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.ProcessManagers.IProcessManagerRepository

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Sagas.ProcessManagers.IProcessManagerStepExecutor

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Capabilities.SecretVaultCapability
files.Summary: The optional capabilities a secret-vault adapter can declare. Consumers use the declared matrix to drive UI affordances and to select providers; adapters use to fail uniformly when an undeclared capability is invoked.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Capabilities.SecretVaultCapabilityLevel
files.Summary: The support level an adapter declares for a .

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Capabilities.SecretVaultCapabilitySupport
files.Summary: An adapter's declared support for a single capability.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Connections.SecretVaultConnection
files.Summary: Everything an adapter needs to reach one vault tenancy on one provider. Passed explicitly to every port method so adapters stay stateless singletons and a single adapter instance can serve many tenancies (platform-owned today, per-tenant or BYO-vault later) without contract changes.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Connections.SecretVaultCredential.ApiToken
files.Summary: A durable API token or key (Scaleway IAM API key secret, Vault token, cloud key-vault access key).

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Connections.SecretVaultCredential.None
files.Summary: No credential material: for in-memory and null vaults, or adapters that authenticate ambiently (workload identity, instance profile).

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Connections.SecretVaultCredential
files.Summary: The credential material of a , as a closed union. Token-bearing members redact their material in ToString() so a logged connection never leaks a secret.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.ISecretVault
files.Summary: The secret-vault facade: one instance per provider adapter, carrying the provider discriminator, the declarative capability matrix, and the concern-scoped ports. Consumers resolve IEnumerable<ISecretVault> and dispatch on (the sub-ports are also registered individually for single-concern consumers).

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.CreateVaultSecret
files.Summary: The request to create a secret container (which holds versions, but no material yet — write the first version with ).

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.SecretMaterial
files.Summary: The payload of one secret version. Wraps the raw bytes so the value can never leak through ToString() (logging, interpolation, exception messages). No zeroing guarantees are made — the .NET GC copies freely — so treat any process that held a material as having seen the plaintext.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.SecretScopePath
files.Summary: A validated hierarchical path (/segment/segment/...) locating a secret inside a vault tenancy. The path is organizational only — callers define their own layout conventions; adapters map it onto the provider's folder/path concept (or a name prefix when the provider has none). The path is never the secret's identity: consumers must address secrets by the provider-side id returned at creation.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.VaultSecretDescriptor
files.Summary: A secret container as the provider reports it. Carries no material.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.VaultSecretVersion
files.Summary: One immutable version of a secret, identified by its monotonically increasing (1-based). A revision number is never reused, which is what makes (secretId, revision) a stable value reference for history and rollback.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Model.VaultSecretVersionStatus
files.Summary: The lifecycle state of a single secret version.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.SecretVaultErrors
files.Summary: Provides standardized error definitions for secret-vault operations. Adapters map provider responses onto these errors so consumers can handle failures uniformly across providers.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Services.ISecretContainerService
files.Summary: Secret container lifecycle: create, describe, list, delete. Containers hold versions (); they carry no material themselves.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Services.ISecretVersionService
files.Summary: Immutable secret versions. Every read addresses an explicit revision — the port has no "latest" concept, deliberately: which revision is current is the caller's metadata, so history stays stable and rollback is a re-pointing of references, independent of provider-side mutable state.

files.Title: Compendium.Abstractions.Secrets.Stubs.NullSecretVault
files.Summary: The fail-fast vault registered when no provider is configured: every operation fails with SecretVault.NotConfigured. Keeps consumers honest — a missing configuration surfaces as a uniform, diagnosable error instead of a null reference or a silent no-op.
